subject: Scaling AI Agents: Data Structures & Real-time Syncs
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was on "Scaling AI Agents: Data Structures & Real-time Syncs"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot about data structures for reliable AI agents and building real-time sync systems for collaborative AI. Here's a quick recap:

*   **Watch out for 'Slop'**: We talked about how even advanced AI models can make surprisingly poor data structure choices. This often leads to what we call 'slop,' where small issues grow quickly and make your code really hard to manage. The best way to fight this? Using strong type systems (like enums) and smart data structures. They're key to keeping things clean and preventing bad states.
*   **Don't Build Your Own Sync System from Scratch**: Building collaborative AI brings a big challenge: keeping lots of different, rapidly changing data in sync across many clients and workers. Think about agent conversations or token streams. Basic methods like constant polling or simple WebSockets usually aren't efficient or scalable enough for this.
*   **Smart Syncing is Key**: Good sync systems know that not all data needs to be handled the same way. We looked at 'slow sync' for structured data, which can use things like database logs, and 'fast sync' for quick updates like streaming tokens, often with dedicated stream servers. This approach helps you update things incrementally and efficiently, giving users a smooth, real-time experience without overloading your servers.

So, what's the main idea from this session?
Basically, if you're not careful with data structures, AI agents can quickly make your code messy and hard to deal with. And for collaborative AI that needs to be real-time, it's usually much better to use existing, proven sync solutions instead of trying to build one from scratch.

If you have any questions, reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
